root_cause.text: The bridge MRP netlink handlers (`br_mrp_start_test()` and `br_mrp_start_in_test()`) accepted a user-controlled `interval` attribute as an unsigned 32-bit value without enforcing a minimum of 1, so `0` propagated into `usecs_to_jiffies(0)` and caused delayed work to reschedule immediately in a tight loop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `IFLA_BRIDGE_MRP_START_TEST_INTERVAL` and `IFLA_BRIDGE_MRP_START_IN_TEST_INTERVAL` from plain `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MIN(NLA_U32, 1)` in `net/bridge/br_mrp_netlink.c`, and the CVE text states that zero “causing the delayed work ... to reschedule itself with zero delay” leads to a “tight loop on system_percpu_wq” and OOM panic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Require a minimum interval of 1 for MRP start-test netlink requests.
intent_record.what: The netlink policy for `IFLA_BRIDGE_MRP_START_TEST_INTERVAL` was changed from a plain `NLA_U32` type declaration to `NLA_POLICY_MIN(NLA_U32, 1)`, adding a minimum accepted value of 1.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the attribute parser will now reject `INTERVAL` values smaller than 1 instead of accepting any 32-bit unsigned integer, preventing zero or invalid interval settings from reaching the MRP start-test logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a minimum-value guard to the MRP start-in-test interval netlink attribute so zero is no longer accepted.
intent_record.what: The netlink policy entry for IFLA_BRIDGE_MRP_START_IN_TEST_INTERVAL was changed from a plain NLA_U32 type declaration to NLA_POLICY_MIN(NLA_U32, 1), adding a minimum accepted value of 1.
intent_record.how: At runtime, parsing of this attribute will now reject zero-valued interval inputs while still accepting 32-bit unsigned integers greater than or equal to 1, preventing invalid test intervals from being configured.

grouping_result.intent: Add a minimum-value guard to the MRP start-in-test interval netlink attribute so zero is no longer accepted.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add a minimum-value guard so the MRP start-test interval netlink attribute no longer accepts zero.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause by adding a minimum-value check so the user-controlled MRP interval attribute cannot be zero in the start-test and start-in-test netlink handlers, preventing the problematic immediate rescheduling behavior.

candidates.rationale: This netlink policy accepted the user-controlled start-test interval as a plain unsigned 32-bit value with no minimum constraint, allowing 0 to reach the timer/work scheduling path.

This netlink policy accepted the user-controlled start-in-test interval as a plain unsigned 32-bit value with no minimum constraint, allowing 0 to propagate into usecs_to_jiffies(0) and trigger immediate rescheduling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This policy entry allowed the start-test interval to be provided as any u32, including 0, which matches the root cause of zero reaching usecs_to_jiffies(0) and causing immediate rescheduling.
This policy entry allowed the start-in-test interval to be provided as any u32, including 0, which matches the root cause of zero reaching usecs_to_jiffies(0) and causing immediate rescheduling.
